safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Increase safety lead time from 0.00 to 1.97 days

narrative: Material PL3__M1A95D48 displays an intermittent demand pattern (CV=0.88) with a pronounced seasonal peak in Q2 2025 and a recovery phase beginning Q1 2026. Lead times are short on average (0.78 days) but highly variable (CV=1.18), with occasional disruptions exceeding 3-4 days — the primary driver of safety stock requirements. A classical (r,Q) EOQ policy with reorder point 481 and order quantity 1816 balances ordering frequency against holding costs while maintaining the 95% service level target. The SAP baseline of zero safety stock is inadequate and should be updated immediately to 345 units with safety lead time set to 1.97 days.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The intermittent regime with moderate volume and a well-defined mean warrants a fixed-quantity (r,Q) policy. EOQ minimises total replenishment and holding cost given the stable ordering cadence, and is robust to the mixed-zero demand distribution observed.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Medium — lead-time spikes up to 4.3 days can temporarily push demand-during-lead-time well above the safety stock buffer. The robust SS of 400 units should be considered if stockouts materialise in practice.
research_insights.escalation_flag: The current SAP safety stock of 0 units and 0-day safety lead time creates a material service risk. Immediate ERP update to SS=345 and safety lead time=1.97 days is strongly recommended.
